ContainedObjects.Description:
Height (base to top): 2.71 in
Old Quarter Excavation R1.
Use actual geometry for line of fire and cover.
ContainedObjects.LuaScript:
function onLoad() self.setLock(true) end
-- BEGIN LOBO BASE-TO-TOP HEIGHT V1
-- Rendered model bounds already include the object's current scale.
-- Project the normalized renderer bounds onto vertical; world elevation is irrelevant.
local loboHeightTimer=nil
local loboHeightPrefix='Height (base to top): '
local function loboHeightBody(description)
 local s=description or ''
 if string.sub(s,1,#loboHeightPrefix)==loboHeightPrefix then
  local e=string.find(s,'\n',1,true)
  return e and string.sub(s,e+1) or ''
 end
 return s
end
local function loboHeightRefresh()
 if self.isDestroyed() or self.loading_custom then return false end
 local ok,bounds=pcall(function() return self.getVisualBoundsNormalized() end)
 if not ok or not bounds or not bounds.size then return false end
 local size=bounds.size
 if not size.x or not size.y or not size.z then return false end
 local right,up,forward=self.getTransformRight(),self.getTransformUp(),self.getTransformForward()
 local height=math.abs(right.y)*size.x+math.abs(up.y)*size.y+math.abs(forward.y)*size.z
 if height~=height or height<=0.001 or height==math.huge then return false end
 local description=loboHeightPrefix..string.format('%.2f in',height)
 local body=loboHeightBody(self.getDescription())
 if body~='' then description=description..'\n'..body end
 if self.getDescription()~=description then self.setDescription(description) end
 self.tooltip=true
 return true
end
local function loboHeightStop()
 if loboHeightTimer then Wait.stop(loboHeightTimer);loboHeightTimer=nil end
end
local function loboHeightBegin()
 loboHeightStop()
 if loboHeightRefresh() then return end
 local tries=0
 loboHeightTimer=Wait.time(function()
  tries=tries+1
  if self.isDestroyed() or loboHeightRefresh() or tries>=90 then loboHeightStop() end
 end,1,90)
end
local loboHeightPreviousLoad=onLoad
function onLoad(saved)
 if loboHeightPreviousLoad then loboHeightPreviousLoad(saved) end
 Wait.frames(loboHeightBegin,2)
end
local loboHeightPreviousState=onStateChange
function onStateChange(oldGuid)
 if loboHeightPreviousState then loboHeightPreviousState(oldGuid) end
 Wait.frames(loboHeightBegin,2)
end
local loboHeightPreviousHover=onHover
function onHover(color)
 if loboHeightPreviousHover then loboHeightPreviousHover(color) end
 loboHeightRefresh()
end
local loboHeightPreviousDestroy=onDestroy
function onDestroy()
 loboHeightStop()
 if loboHeightPreviousDestroy then loboHeightPreviousDestroy() end
end
-- END LOBO BASE-TO-TOP HEIGHT V1

ContainedObjects.LuaScript:
-- Universal DZ compositor: preserve mission lines while owning deployment visibility.
local function loboUniversalWrite(target,lines)
 if target.getGUID()=="5ffe17" then
  local owner=getObjectFromGUID("707e8b")
  if owner and not owner.isDestroyed() then
   local ok,handled=pcall(function()return owner.call('loboUniversalSetBase',{guid=target.getGUID(),lines=lines})end)
   if ok and handled then return end
  end
 end
 target.setVectorLines(lines)
end
-- BEGIN LOBO CONTRAST DEPLOYMENT LINES V2
-- Every colored centerline remains at its exact measured X/Z coordinates.
local function loboContrastDraw(target,source)
 if not target or target.isDestroyed() then return end
 local strokes={}
 for _,line in ipairs(source or {}) do
  if line.points and #line.points>1 then
   local width=math.max((tonumber(line.thickness) or .015)*1.5,.065)
   local border,core={},{}
   for k,v in pairs(line) do border[k]=v;core[k]=v end
   border.color={.006,.009,.014}
   border.thickness=width+.085
   core.thickness=width
   local c=line.color or {1,1,1}
   local r,g,b=c.r or c[1] or 1,c.g or c[2] or 1,c.b or c[3] or 1
   local maximum=math.max(r,g,b,.001)
   r,g,b=r/maximum,g/maximum,b/maximum
   if b>r*1.5 and b>g then g=math.max(g,.82);r=math.min(r,.18)
   elseif r>b*1.5 and r>=g then
    if g>.7 then g=math.max(g,.95);b=math.min(b,.12)
    else g=math.max(g,.55);b=math.min(b,.16) end
   end
   core.color={r,g,b}
   core.points={}
   for _,p in ipairs(line.points) do
    local world=target.positionToWorld(Vector(p.x or p[1],p.y or p[2],p.z or p[3]))
    world.y=world.y+.004
    local q=target.positionToLocal(world)
    core.points[#core.points+1]={q.x,q.y,q.z}
   end
   strokes[#strokes+1]=border
   strokes[#strokes+1]=core
  end
 end
 loboUniversalWrite(target,strokes)
end
-- END LOBO CONTRAST DEPLOYMENT LINES V2

 if loboLifeDead or self.isDestroyed() then return false end
 if loboLifeAnchor then
  local anchor=getObjectFromGUID(loboLifeAnchor)
  if loboLifeWasPlaced and (not anchor or anchor.isDestroyed()) then return false end
  local p=self.getPosition()

local function loboLifeGetBroker()
 if loboLifeBroker and not loboLifeBroker.isDestroyed() then return loboLifeBroker end
 local guid=Global.getVar('LoboMapUIBrokerV4')
 local broker=guid and getObjectFromGUID(guid) or nil
 if not broker then
  for _,candidate in ipairs(getObjectsWithTag('LoboMapUIBrokerV4') or {}) do broker=candidate;break end
 end

  broker=spawnObjectData({data=JSON.decode(loboLifeBrokerData)})
  if broker then Global.setVar('LoboMapUIBrokerV4',broker.getGUID()) end
 end
 loboLifeBroker=broker;return broker
end
local function loboLifeCall(name,p)
 local broker=loboLifeBroker
 if not broker or broker.isDestroyed() or not loboLifeToken then return nil end
 p=p or {};p.owner=loboLifeOwner;p.token=loboLifeToken
 return broker.call(name,p)
end

local function loboLifeStop(id)
 if id and loboLifeWaits[id] then loboNativeWait.stop(id);loboLifeWaits[id]=nil end
end
local function loboLifeGuard(fn)
 return function(...) if loboLifeAlive() then return fn(...) end end
end

function Wait.time(fn,delay,repetitions)
 local id
 id=loboNativeWait.time(function()
  if not loboLifeAlive() then loboLifeStop(id);return end
  if not repetitions or repetitions==1 then loboLifeWaits[id]=nil end

local rules=[[THE DIG — ITS SEASON 18
Mission reference: Infinity Mission Geist
https://infinitygeist.com/mission/s18_the_dig
Scenario based on Robert Shepherd's The Monday Signal mission.

MISSION OVERVIEW
Reinforcements-compatible. Retreat! applies. Each player uses one HVT and two Classified Objectives. Each completed Classified is worth 1 OP.

SCORING — MAXIMUM 10 OP
• Neutralize an already-analysed Hyperthermal Tech: 2 OP per Tech, up to three Techs / 6 OP.
• At game end, if you neutralized at least one Tech in every Game Round: 1 OP.
• At game end, if more Consoles carry your Player Token than the opponent's: 1 OP.
• Two Classified Objectives: 1 OP each.

DEPLOYMENT AND CONSOLES — THIS MAP
This is the 48 × 48 inch, 300-point setup. Players deploy in opposite corner zones, each measured as a 24-inch radius from its corner. Neither player may deploy a trooper in Silhouette contact with a Console or Hyperthermal Tech.

There are three Consoles on the other diagonal: one at table centre, and one 16 inches in each direction from centre. Use Console A tokens or 40 mm diameter objective scenery. The familiar consoles supplied with this map have 40 mm mission footprints.

The Deployment menu can show 24-, 28- and 32-inch corner arcs independently. Side A (blue) and Side B (orange) can be selected separately, together, or hidden. The 24-inch arcs define the actual Deployment Zones. The 28-/32-inch arcs are +4-/+8-inch measuring aids; displaying them does not enlarge the mission's Deployment Zones or change Tech-placement restrictions. Apply the relevant troop's deployment rules normally.

HYPERTHERMAL DIG — BEFORE ARMY DEPLOYMENT
Each player places three Hyperthermal Tech tokens. The player who kept Deployment places their three first.

Use 25 mm diameter Tech tokens or equivalent scenery. The WHOLE token must be more than 8 inches from BOTH players' Deployment Zones and from every other Tech token. It must be on accessible table ground, never on top of or inside scenery or a building. In a 150-point game these two spacing requirements are 4 inches instead.

Use the normal Infinity mod Hyperthermal Tech markers for player placement; this map creates no Tech models. Players choose positions that satisfy the restrictions above.

ANALYZE HYPERTHERMAL TECH
Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario.

Who and where:
• A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console that does not already have that player's own Player Token.

Resolution:
• Make a Normal WIP Roll. After failure, another attempt is allowed by spending another Short Skill.
• On success, remove the opponent's Player Token beside that Console and mark it for the active player.
• If the active player's total of analysed or neutralized Tech is still below three, the opponent chooses ANY currently unanalysed Tech token on the board to become analysed for the active player.
• Use distinguishable Player A/B tokens to show which player owns the Console and the analysed Tech. The choice of Tech belongs to the opponent, not to the Specialist's owner.

NEUTRALIZE HYPERTHERMAL TECH
Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario.

Any trooper may perform this task, provided it is in Silhouette contact with an analysed Tech bearing its OWN player's token. No roll is required. Remove that Tech token from the table after neutralization.

SPECIALIST TROOPS
For this mission: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and troops with Chain of Command or Specialist Operative.

Repeaters and Peripheral (Servant) models cannot be used by Hackers, Doctors or Engineers to carry out tasks that require a Specialist Troop.

OPERATIONAL LEARNING
After a Specialist fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, continuing the SAME task in consecutive Orders gives:
• Second consecutive Order: +3 WIP.
• Third consecutive Order and later consecutive Orders: +3 WIP and +1SD.
These bonuses combine with other applicable Scenario-skill MODs.

The same Specialist must keep using the same Scenario Skill against the same target, without interruption. A successful roll, using a different Skill, changing target, or spending an Order on another trooper resets the sequence. Only one sequence may apply to a trooper for a given Scenario Skill at a time.

END OF THE MISSION
Play ends after the third Game Round. If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, the game finishes at the end of that turn.

OTHER POINT LEVELS IN MISSION GEIST
• 300 / 350 / 400 points: 48 × 48 table; 24-inch corner zones.
• 200 / 250 points: 32 × 48 table; 20-inch corner zones.
• 150 points: 24 × 32 table; 12-inch corner zones; 4-inch Tech spacing.
This terrain remains the 48 × 48 setup; overlay selections do not resize it.

CURRENT WORDING
The task previously called Activate Console is Analyze Hyperthermal Tech. Console ownership and neutralization use Player Tokens; neutralization requires a Tech analysed for your own player. The small-game spacing exception applies at 150 points.

TERRAIN & ACCESS
Use the modeled geometry for line of fire and cover. The three open excavation pockets are 2.5 inches below street level and are 8 by 7 inches with two staggered ramps apiece; there is no tunnel network. Buildings have usable interiors and roofs. Taller buildings: state 1 roof on, state 2 upper floor exposed, state 3 ground floor exposed. Single-storey buildings: state 1 roof on, state 2 ground floor exposed. External roof ladders persist in all states. Rubble has no automatic special terrain effect.

local function textHeight(text,width,size)
 -- TTS rejects the former long-string gmatch pattern ("pattern too complex").
 -- Only literal searches are used here, as in the working campaign controls.
 local chars=math.floor(width/(size*.54));local lines=0;local first=1
 while true do
  local last=string.find(text,'\n',first,true)
  local count=(last or (#text+1))-first
  lines=lines+math.max(1,math.ceil(count/chars))
  if not last then break end
  first=last+1
 end
 return math.max(590,lines*(size+7)+30)
end
